entries.snippet: Residents of Georgia's 13th Congressional District outside of Atlanta will get a new representative to Congress after a special election runoff Tuesday to replace the late Democratic Rep. David Scott, who died April 22.

entries.snippet: The U.S. Postal Service laid out how it would implement the order last week, but time is running short to impose major changes with some states beginning to send mail ballots to voters in just a few weeks.

entries.title: U.S. set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
entries.snippet: The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States.

entries.title: U.S. border reopens to Mexican cattle imports, but economists doubt the move will reduce high beef prices

entries.title: WATCH: Forensic psychologist testifies that Lindsay Clancy has bipolar disorder
entries.snippet: Kirk Heilbrun, who examined Clancy over three days this year, said he struggled to reach a diagnosis of bipolar 2 disorder "because of all the diagnoses in the records and all the symptoms that she experienced."

entries.title: Taiwan charges 9 over illegal AI server exports to China, including Nvidia and Super Micro staffers
entries.snippet: Taiwanese prosecutors charged nine people Monday for illegally exporting "high-end AI servers" to mainland China, adding another wave of turbulence in the AI rivalry between China and the United States.

entries.title: US announces bid to further isolate Iran economically
entries.snippet: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has outlined what he called "unprecedented" moves to isolate Iran economically. He said it will focus on third countries, warning those who don't comply will "share" in the isolation.

entries.title: DR Congo peace roadmap: Will the fighting finally end?
entries.snippet: A new roadmap sets out the conditions toward peace in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). But disagreements over M23 rebels, Rwanda's role and security concerns remain, and could still derail the process.

entries.title: The new Bundesliga season is here, but has the glow gone?
entries.snippet: Another Bundesliga season arrives, but are the golden years of Germany's top football league already over, and what can it do to change its course?

entries.title: Trump says Canada to face 50% auto, steel tariffs from 2027
entries.snippet: The latest threat comes after the neighbors failed to reach a deal to avert a 50% US levy on a range of other Canadian goods. Ottawa says it plans to impose retaliatory tariffs.

entries.title: Iran protest victim: 'They were shooting to kill'
entries.snippet: DW spoke with several Iranians affected by a brutal crackdown at the hands of the Tehran's security forces during the height of massive public protests in January.

entries.title: Myanmar: Why Rohingya refugees can't return
entries.snippet: Nine years after the Rohingya were driven from Myanmar, claims of progress on refugee returns have revived talk of repatriation.

entries.title: Star violinist Anne-Sophie Mutter: 50 years on stage
entries.snippet: Anne-Sophie Mutter constantly reinvents herself. For her 50th onstage anniversary, the star violinist is surprising audiences with sounds from around the world and never-before-recorded commissions.

entries.title: Syria sentences Assad-era top Muslim cleric to life in prison
entries.snippet: Muslim cleric Ahmad Hassoun was convicted of crimes including inciting sectarian violence and justifying murder. He is the latest Syrian official aligned with ousted President Bashar Assad to face trial.

entries.title: Dutch pull out of 'no longer neutral' Eurovision
entries.snippet: The Netherlands will not participate in the 2027 Eurovision Song Contest in Bulgaria, the state broadcaster has said, citing divisions over the situation in Gaza. It's the second time the country is boycotting the event.

entries.title: Scientists discover new 'immune hubs' in skull bone marrow
entries.snippet: In mouse skull marrow, 'immune hubs' that actively defend the brain have been discovered. Similar cells exist in human skulls, but their role remains unclear.

entries.title: Spiraling health costs force Iranians to delay care
entries.snippet: A single chemotherapy session in Iran can cost six times the monthly minimum wage. As drug prices soar and medicine is in short supply, doctors say more patients are delaying or abandoning treatment.

entries.title: India news: Police used 'excessive force' on CJP protesters
entries.snippet: Amnesty International alleges that police in the capital New Delhi and the state of Bihar used excessive force against youth-led Cockroach protesters. Full details and more in DW's roundup of major headlines in India.

entries.title: Germany news: State premier visits VW for crisis talks
entries.snippet: Lower Saxony's state premier called on Volkswagen shareholders to take action to avert plant closures, while Chancellor Friedrich Merz met party colleagues after a testing summer.

entries.title: Burnham likens Ukraine fight to British stand against Nazis
entries.snippet: Andy Burnham's first trip abroad as prime minister includes co-chairing a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing and holding talks with Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The visit comes on Ukraine's Independence Day.

entries.title: New Zealand proposes social media ban for under-16s
entries.snippet: The government is set to follow Australia's lead and introduce a bill banning children from social media. But the plan already faces opposition from within the ruling coalition.

entries.title: US: Wildfire forces mass evacuations near Reno, Nevada
entries.snippet: A wind-driven wildfire has forced roughly 42,000 people to evacuate and destroyed homes as fire crews continue to battle extreme conditions.

entries.title: Norway: King Harald's health has 'deteriorated,' palace says
entries.snippet: The 89-year-old King of Norway is Europe's oldest reigning monarch. He has been suffering from a blood condition.

entries.title: Kazakhstan parliamentary vote cements president's power
entries.snippet: Candidates from seven state-approved parties took part in the election, while opposition parties were banned. As Central Asia's largest nation, Kazakhstan maintains a delicate balance between Russia and the West.

entries.title: Zelenskyy repeats Ukraine not behind Nord Stream attack
entries.snippet: Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was assisting German authorities with their investigation into the Nord Stream explosions. A second Ukrainian national was arrested in connection with the blasts.
